source: Spitschan M, Aguirre GK, Brainard DH, Sweeney AM (2016). Variation of outdoor illumination as a function of solar elevation and light pollution. Scientific Reports 6: 26756, doi:10.1038/srep26756 (correction: Sci Rep 7: 46930, 2017)
quantity: absolute downwelling spectral irradiance (radiance x pi, paper Methods)
timestamp_format: dd-MMM-yyyy HH:mm:ss, as in the source; no time zone in the source
wavelength_source: the source CSVs have no wavelength row; rows 6-566 = 280-840 nm at 1 nm per the IlluminationSpectraDataset README (Table S1) and data/raw/spectra/MANIFEST.csv; 561 rows are consistent with this
night_id_note: night_id = source row 2 ("date/night") as published. It changes at about 01:05 (source time) inside one continuous night, so one night of measuring can carry two ids (8 ids over 5 night blocks per site). Not used by the app.
source_column_note: source_column in the site files is 1-based: column 1 = the first spectrum column of the source CSV; the irradiance at wavelength w is in CSV row 6 + (w - 280)
verbatim: every number taken from the source is written as its source text

selection.label: inferred
selection.rule: solar elevation < -18 deg; then 240 spectra evenly sampled in source column order (index round_half_up(i*(n-1)/239)); every 2nd wavelength 280-840 nm; values verbatim
selection.rules_from: human decisions in handoff 2026-10-04_two-nights-spectra.md (reproducing the draft "3D Spectrum" view)

display_limits_log10.label: inferred
display_limits_log10.rule: over all selected values > 0 of both sites: floor(p01), ceil(p99) of log10(value); linear-interpolation percentile, index (N-1)*q
